content:
Meta AI glasses have been receiving extremely poor reviews recently. So poor, in fact, that one of the top three paid apps on the US iPhone App Store today is specifically designed to detect who nearby might be wearing smart glasses.

The app's name leaves nothing to the imagination—it's called "Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner," and it claims to detect and alert you when someone nearby is wearing Meta AI glasses.

Many iPhone users have already paid US$3 to try it out, and the app has temporarily climbed to third place on the US iPhone paid App Store rankings. It's rare for a new paid app to break into these rankings.

We haven't tested the app ourselves to see if it actually works, and even if it does work, it's still unclear what you should actually do once it detects someone wearing AI glasses.

At this stage, smart glasses equipped with cameras are still fairly easy to spot, so you might not actually need an app to tell you who's wearing them.

Still, public dissatisfaction is already very apparent. Many people are highly averse to the very concept of AI smart glasses, feeling it raises privacy concerns. If Apple wants to enter the smart glasses arena next year, this represents a significant obstacle.
